waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

provider_policy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

Which system of record assigns the authoritative identifier for this contact point, and does that identifier remain stable when the endpoint value changes?
Is the contact-point identifier globally resolvable, or unique only within the owning party's record?
What distinguishes the contact-point record identity from the endpoint value that natural-key strategies would otherwise use?
How are two contact-point records that normalize to the same endpoint value for the same party reconciled?
Which party does this contact point belong to, and under which identifier scheme is that party referenced?
Can this endpoint be shared by more than one party, and how is shared or delegated use represented?
Who is authorized to add, change or retire a contact point on behalf of the owning party?
Is this contact point held for a role or function rather than for a named natural person, and how is that flagged?
Which addressing scheme governs the syntax of this endpoint value, and which specification defines that scheme?
Is the endpoint kind derivable from the value itself, or must it be declared independently of the stored value?
Which code list is authoritative for endpoint kind, and how are emerging or unregistered channel types admitted?
What happens when a value is syntactically valid under more than one scheme, such as a digit string usable as both a telephone number and a messaging handle?
For which use contexts or business purposes is this endpoint intended, and are multiple contexts simultaneously applicable?
Which technical capabilities does the endpoint support, and were those capabilities declared by the party or observed by a system?
Does recording a purpose context here imply any permission to contact the party for that purpose?
Which geographic or linguistic service scope applies to this contact point?
Is the stored number a global E.164 number, or a local number that requires a phone-context to be unambiguous?
What is the canonical machine form of this telephone endpoint, and which characters are significant when two numbers are compared?
How is the human-readable display form derived, and which notation standard governs its spacing and symbols?
How are extensions, dialling prefixes and subaddresses represented without corrupting the canonical number?
Which portion of this mailbox may be case-folded during normalization and which portion must be preserved exactly as supplied?
Does this mailbox contain non-ASCII characters in the local part, in the domain, or in both?
Is an ASCII fallback address recorded, and on whose authority is it treated as equivalent to the internationalized address?
How is the domain part recorded when both A-label and U-label forms exist for the same name?
Which URI scheme and authority identify this endpoint, and is the recorded URI absolute rather than relative?
Which normalization steps may be applied before two URI endpoints are treated as equivalent?
When a messaging handle is recorded without a resolvable URI, which service identifier disambiguates the handle?
Does this endpoint address the party directly, or a publicly readable profile that third parties also observe?
Which addressed location does this postal contact point designate, and by which reference is that location identified?
Which country template and postal component set govern rendition of this address for delivery?
Which delivery-specific attributes belong to the contact point rather than to the location itself?
Is the delivery point a place the party occupies, or purely a mail-receipt arrangement such as a box or forwarding agent?
Which Unicode normalization form is required before an endpoint value is stored or compared?
Which language tag applies to the human-readable label for this endpoint?
How are localized alternative forms of one endpoint recorded without creating duplicate contact points?
Which script or transliteration variant is authoritative when a source system supplies more than one?
Which authority asserted that the owning party controls this endpoint, and at what instant was the assertion made?
Which verification method class and assurance level does the assertion claim?
Does the assertion expire, and which events invalidate it before its stated expiry?
Which system executed the proofing challenge, and where is the audit record of that execution held?
From which instant until which instant is this contact point valid for use by the owning party?
Which lifecycle state does the contact point currently hold, and which state transitions are permitted from it?
Is a recorded end date an assertion of past fact or a scheduled future change, and how is a still-open interval represented?
Are there recurring windows within the validity interval during which the contact point is available or restricted?
What is the last recorded reachability status of this endpoint and at which instant was it observed?
Which evidence supports the recorded reachability status, and in which model is that evidence held?
Does an unreachable status invalidate the contact point, or only suppress its operational use?
Who may set or override reachability status, and may it be set without an underlying observation?
Which contact point replaces this one, and from which effective instant does the replacement apply?
Is a superseded contact point retained for historical interpretation, or disposed once the successor is active?
How is a supersession chain traversed to obtain the currently effective endpoint for a historical reference?
What prevents a supersession cycle or a fork with two concurrent successors?
Which communication purpose classes does this statement govern, and is the class list closed or extensible?
Which usage context qualifies the statement, and what does an absent context mean?
How is an inbound contact request handled when it declares no purpose class at all?
Which capacity does the statement cover when the same party acts as customer, employee and emergency contact?
Which profile-conditional situations must be recorded explicitly instead of being inferred as defaults?
Which channel kinds are declared preferred within this scope, and how is the preference value expressed numerically?
What does an absent preference value mean, and may a single valued instance be read on its own?
Are preference values comparable between different channel kinds, or only within the same kind?
Which channel-kind or endpoint reference does the statement point to, and how is a reference that no longer resolves treated?
Which combination of channel, purpose, context and time does the party ask to avoid, and at what precision is that combination stated?
How is this advisory statement distinguished in data from the legally governed restriction record held in the external registry?
Can this statement ever widen the set of permitted options relative to an external restriction?
What firmness does the party attach to the request, and how is that recorded without implying legal weight?
For how long does the request stay effective, and does it expire by default?
Which language tags does the party prefer for written and for spoken interaction, and in what order?
When must a script subtag be carried on a preference tag, and when should it be omitted?
Does the language preference differ by usage context, and how are competing per-context orders reconciled?
What is the correct behaviour when no preferred language can be produced on the selected channel?
Which locale formatting conventions travel with a language preference, and which stay with the rendering system?
Which functional accommodation directives apply to communication with this party, inbound and outbound?
How is the directive expressed so that it states a functional need without disclosing or implying a diagnosis?
Which channel capabilities must a candidate option possess before the directive counts as satisfiable?
What must happen when no available channel can satisfy the accommodation directive?
Which record is the authoritative source of this directive when an external accessibility profile also exists?
Which time-zone identifier governs interpretation of this party's stated windows?
Why is a fixed UTC offset insufficient for a stated window, and in which narrow case may one still be recorded?
How are time-zone database releases and renamed or linked zone identifiers handled as the registry changes?
How is the party's habitual zone distinguished from a temporary zone assumed during travel?
Which recurring pattern expresses the party's stated contactable periods, and in which time-zone frame is it read?
Is time not covered by any declared window contactable or not contactable by default?
How is a single-occurrence exception expressed without rewriting the underlying pattern?
Does a stated window assert anything about the party's actual calendar availability at that time?
What granularity and minimum duration make a stated window meaningful for routing?
How is a total order derived when several candidate options carry equal or absent preference values?
Which condition moves routing to the next option in the sequence, and which component evaluates that condition?
Has the party stated a maximum number of attempts or a minimum interval between them?
How does the fallback sequence change with purpose class and urgency tier?
Which urgency tiers are recognised for this profile, and against which vocabulary are they defined?
Which of the party's own statements may an urgency tier override, and which may it never override?
Which requesting roles are permitted to assert the highest urgency tier on an outbound request?
Has life-safety routing been declared for this party, and how is its absence interpreted?
What is the outcome when a high urgency tier meets an active external communication restriction?
Which party is designated as delegate or alternate, and by which reference into the party model?
Which registered relation type qualifies the designation, and from which registry is it drawn?
For which purpose classes and urgency tiers is the designation valid, and does it replace or supplement contacting the party?
What authority supports the designation, and where is that evidence held?
When does the designation lapse, and what happens to routing already in flight at that moment?
What effective interval bounds this statement, and what does an open-ended end mean?
How does a temporary override supersede a standing statement without deleting it?

Which statement applies at an instant when several overrides are effective at once?
How long is a superseded statement retained so that a past outcome remains explainable?

Which input may only narrow the result, and which input blocks an option outright?
What must be returned when the external communication-restriction reference cannot be resolved at evaluation time?
How is a genuine contradiction between two statements of equal precedence surfaced rather than silently resolved?
Which edition of the precedence ruleset produced a given resolution, and how is that recorded on the result?
Who asserted this preference, the party or an authorised steward, and under what authority did they act?
Through which capture channel was the statement made, and what assurance level does that channel carry?
How are the instant of statement and the instant of recording represented when they differ?
Which statements may an operator alter on the party's behalf, and what must be recorded when they do?
How does the advisory resolver treat a statement whose provenance or assurance is weak?
On what recorded mandate may an agent other than the data subject assert or change this contact point?
How is a self-asserted change by the data subject distinguished from a steward-asserted or system-derived change?
Which contact-point operations does the mandate permit and which does it explicitly exclude?

Which external authorisation model renders the allow or deny decision, and what decision reference is retained here?
Which system of record is authoritative for this contact point, and which systems hold non-authoritative copies?
Which named steward role is accountable for the accuracy and currency of this contact point?
Which party acts as controller and which as processor for this contact point, and does that differ by purpose?
How is a change of owning system or steward recorded without losing the prior chain of responsibility?
Which activity generated this contact-point value, and from what upstream entity was it derived?
What are the separate event time, observation time and record-ingestion time for this assertion?
To which responsible agent is the assertion attributed, and with what qualification?
What reliability grade is attached to the originating source, and how was that grade derived?
By what method and at what assurance was control of this endpoint demonstrated?
When did the successful verification occur, and when does the verification state expire or require renewal?
What must never be persisted in this model from the verification exchange?
How are failed, abandoned or replayed verification attempts represented without leaking attempt detail?
How is verified control kept distinct from lawful permission to contact the endpoint?
Which external consent or legal-basis record authorises use of this endpoint for a named purpose?
At what granularity does a permission bind: party, endpoint, channel, purpose or campaign class?
Which restriction, objection or suppression entries currently block use of this endpoint, and who owns them?
How does this model detect that a referenced permission has been withdrawn, expired or superseded?
What consent detail must never be copied into this model?
What is the closed set of lifecycle states for a contact point, and which transitions between them are permitted?
Over what real-world interval is this contact point asserted to be valid, independent of when the record was written?
How is record-time history preserved when a value is corrected rather than genuinely changed?
What opaque version token identifies the current revision for optimistic concurrency?
When one contact point supersedes another, how is the predecessor kept resolvable?
Which syntactic and referential validations must a candidate endpoint pass before it can reach the active state?
What canonical normalised form is stored for matching, and is the original input preserved verbatim?
What matching rule and threshold decide that two contact points denote the same endpoint?
When sources conflict, which value survives and on what recorded justification?
How can an incorrect merge be reversed without destroying either original assertion?
Which observable signals reduce confidence that an endpoint still reaches the intended party?
At what age or consecutive-failure count must an endpoint be re-verified or suspended?
How is a jurisdiction-specific reassignment check recorded, including the reference date used for the query?
When an endpoint is reported compromised or misdirected, what immediate state change is applied here and what is delegated?
What sensitivity classification applies to this contact point, and what drives that classification?
Which purpose makes each stored field necessary, and which fields must be dropped when that purpose ends?
How is an at-risk or protected endpoint flagged so that it is never disclosed or printed by default?
Which contact attributes could reveal special-category or otherwise protected information by inference?
Which fields are released to a requester operating under a stated purpose and role?
How are withheld values represented: omitted, masked, tokenised or replaced by a proxy endpoint?
What must a subject-facing export contain, and which governance fields are excluded from it?
How is a partial or refused disclosure communicated so the requester can act without learning what was hidden?
Which retention schedule or disposition authority sets the keeping period for this contact point?
When erasure is required, is the value destroyed, anonymised or suppressed, and what evidence of the action is kept?
What tombstone remains after deletion so that inbound references resolve without re-exposing the endpoint?
How is a conflict between an erasure request and a legal hold or statutory retention duty resolved and recorded?
Which recipients must be told of a rectification or erasure, and how is that notification evidenced?
What preconditions must hold before a write to a contact point is accepted?
How is a lost update prevented when two agents edit the same profile concurrently?
How is a retried create or delete recognised as the same logical request?
What patch semantics apply to partial edits, and how are they made all-or-nothing?
What audit reference must every accepted mutation return, and who stores the audit entry?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
